tagline: A systematic framework for diagnosing and recovering from catastrophic layer sensitivity in transformers — validated on GPT-2, scaling to Mistral-7B and Llama-3-8B.
phase_status: Phase 11 complete (GPT-2 real GPU validation). Winning Ticket found at 30% sparsity. Next: Llama-3-8B and Mistral-7B on dual 3090 remote server.
research_question: Can temporal importance metrics — cheap proxy signals computed from gradient dynamics — reliably identify and exploit layer-level elasticity to achieve lossless (< 5% PPL) structured compression at 50%+ parameter reduction without retraining?

overview.title: What we're building
overview.body: A structured pruning + activation healing pipeline (TIM-MGDT) that identifies which transformer layers are elastic vs critical, prunes the elastic ones, and heals the activation drift — recovering perplexity while cutting parameters, latency, and memory by ~50%.

overview.title: Why this matters
overview.body: Existing pruning methods either destroy quality or require expensive retraining. We discovered that Layer 10 in GPT-2 is elastic, not broken — the +108% PPL explosion on hard removal shows over-weighting, not architectural damage. A 2% scaling fix restores balance. TIM-MGDT exploits this insight systematically.

overview.title: Where we are today
overview.body: Phase 11 complete for Mistral-7B. We achieved 19.6% sparsity with only +2.54% PPL degradation! We discovered that constant mean-shift Activation Healing destroys modern LLMs due to RMSNorm scaling conflicts. We successfully pivoted to Masked Sparse Fine-Tuning (SFT). Llama-3-8B is currently running on the dual 3090s.

decisions.rationale: +108% PPL on hard removal = over-weighting. 2% scaling restores it. This insight drives the entire compression strategy.
+4.9% PPL only. Above 30%, PPL degrades rapidly (+21.3% at 40%) — classic phase transition boundary verified.

We proved mathematically that adding a constant mean shift to hidden states inflates the RMS denominator in RMSNorm layers. This crushes the actual signal magnitude. We pivoted to Masked Sparse Fine-Tuning.

decisions.choice: MHA is destructive; GQA will be far more tolerant
decisions.rationale: GPT-2 MHA: +59.3% PPL at 20% head pruning. Llama/Mistral GQA (8 KV groups for 32 Q heads) has built-in query redundancy → much safer.
Standard LM evaluation. Spearman ρ > 0.7 for proxy-to-ground-truth correlation. P-value < 0.05 for statistical significance.
We exclusively use a dual RTX 3090 setup. We do not use Apple MLX or external A100s, enforcing the constraint for our Hardware Memory Wall thesis.

tasks.next_action: Phase 11 and 12 are complete. We proved full-parameter SFT hits a memory wall. Currently running Phase 12.5 SVD-Initialized LoRA recovery sweep.
Activation Healing failed due to RMSNorm. Rewrote Stage 4 to use Masked Sparse Fine-Tuning (SFT) to recover PPL without destroying unstructured sparsity.
Automated dashboard deployed via GitHub Pages. Added a post-run Python hook to automatically update state.json upon run completion.

bulletproofing.item: Phase 6 validation on 500-sample WikiText-2 — -0.11% PPL improvement confirmed.
Phase 5.1 hard pruning baseline — +108% PPL explosion (expected) establishes failure mode.
Phase 11 GPT-2 winning ticket — 30% sparsity, +4.9% PPL only, verified on real GPU.
PyTorch reparameterization quirk documented — weight_orig vs weight after remove_global_pruning.
Conv1D vs nn.Linear healing behavior explained — GPT-2 is architectural edge case.
Llama-3-8B causal patching — expect bell-shaped recovery curve (layers 12-24 critical).
Mistral-7B GQA head pruning — expect much higher tolerance than GPT-2 MHA.
Activation healing on 7B — proven mathematically incompatible with RMSNorm architectures.
InAttention integration with winning-ticket masks for real hardware latency reduction.
KL divergence proxy for 100x profiling speedup on 7B models.
